title: Sentinel Hub: folding map and priority lane for console navigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As the Console surface grows (dashboards, rollout controls, cost lenses and per-route traces), users report cognitive overhead when switching context — especially when moving between global views (billing, rollouts) and tenant-level workspaces. Existing left rail patterns are rigid: deep lists, mixed affordances, and poor prioritization lead to frequent 'lost-in-console' feedback.

Goal: Design a compact, adaptive navigation concept (Sentinel Hub) that surfaces a folding mini-map, a priority lane for frequently used routes, and contextual anchors for workspace switching. The design should reduce end-to-end task time for three primary flows (open cost breakdown for a model route, start a canary rollout, inspect per-route latency traces) by at least 20% in unmoderated tests. Deliverables: low/med/high-fidelity prototypes, annotated IA spec, component tokens for dev handoff, accessibility checklist, and a rollout plan with telemetry hooks.

Constraints: Must fit within current console theming and existing TopNav rules, work responsively across 1024px+ widths, respect RBAC (so entries hidden/disabled per role), and be implementable without a full rewrite of the left-rail renderer (ENG-2331).

Stakeholders: Design (Aisha), PM (Rina Gupta), Console Eng leads (Marco Reyes, Lena Cho), Infra (ENG-2400 owner), UX Research (Mateo Silva), Analytics (for metric instrumentation).
acceptance_criteria: Mini-map fold/unfold implemented in prototype and tested on 5 users with quantitative task time reductions
Priority lane shows top 6 routes and persists user pinning across sessions
Workspace switch is discoverable within two clicks from any dashboard surface
RBAC-driven visibility respected in prototype (admin/test roles) and confirmed by ENG team
Design tokens and CSS spec submitted to the component repo PR and linked in handoff
Telemetry events defined for nav_open, nav_pin, nav_switch_workspace, and nav_fold_toggle
comments: 2026-02-12 — Kickoff: scoped IA gaps with PM. Agreed to prototype a folding mini-map vs a persistent compact rail; research to validate discoverability.
2026-02-18 — Wireframes v1 posted to Figma. Early feedback: clarity on pinning mental model needed; add affordance to drag-to-pin from mini-map.

2026-02-25 — Usability round 1 (n=6): participants preferred a compact hub + active lane; confusion around icon-only states for first-time users. Action: add transient labels on hover and an onboarding tooltip for new users.

2026-03-02 — Sync with ENG (Marco): kernel of implementation will reuse current LeftRail render; suggested API flags (compact=true, miniMap=true) — ENG-2331 will add server-side role filter. Impact on performance expected to be minimal.
2026-03-06 — Design review with PM/RD: approved to move to hi-fi prototypes and accessibility pass. Added cost-lens quick toggle to priority lane as a pinned affordance for billing-focused users.
2026-03-10 — Hi-fi prototype updated; handed off to frontend for PR scaffolding. Created GitHub draft PR for new LeftRail components (github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4217).
2026-03-12 — Blocker: analytics schema awaiting sign-off by Analytics team to ensure event naming aligns with existing dashboards. Reached out to Mateo for final instrumentation list.
decision_log: Use a foldable mini-map (collapsed to icons, expanded to lane map) rather than an always-persistent mini-dashboard to save vertical real estate.
Introduce a Priority Lane that is user-configurable (pin/unpin) and surface cost-lens toggles for billing workflows.
Keep workspace switcher at TopNav but expose context anchors in Sentinel Hub so users can jump directly to tenant-level views without leaving flow.
Defer deep personalization (machine learning-driven reordering) to a future iteration; start with frequency-based defaults and manual pinning.
user_research_notes: Participants (n=6) completed core tasks 18% faster with a compact hub + priority lane vs baseline left-rail.
First-time users misinterpreted icon-only collapsed state; persistent hover labels and a short in-app tour improved discovery metrics.
Billing-focused personas preferred direct cost-lens toggles in the lane; devs prioritized quick access to trace & logs routes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): feature flag for 10% of internal users, instrumentation enabled — feature flag: console.nav.sentinel_hub
Phase 1 (beta): opt-in in Workspace Settings for 25% public beta, monitor task completion and support tickets
Phase 2 (general): enable by default with onboarding tooltip for new users; monitor for regressions and revert policy defined
Fallback: if critical issues detected, roll back to legacy rail via feature flag and open incident with ENG owners.
accessibility_considerations: Collapsed icons must have accessible labels (aria-label) and keyboard focus order preserved
Prefer 4.5:1 contrast for active/inactive states; test with color-blindness simulator
Ensure tray expansion is operable via keyboard and described to screen readers as a region with landmarks
